newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close up, but fail to beat 2,200.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close up, but fail to beat 2,200.

text.p: Dealers said strong interest in property stocks, notably Hongkong Land, helped Singapore shares push higher on Thursday, but not enough to sustain the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index above 2,220 at the close.
"The market is trying to break through this barrier (2,220) at every opportunity it gets," a dealer said.
The STII closed up 3.41 points at 2,197.69 after hitting a high of 2,204.74 and spending much of the day above 2,200.
Hongkong Land was the day's dominant performer with 13.53 million units traded. The stock closed up U.S.$0.31 at US$2.78,
Dealers said interest in the stock, which is included in the newly-launched Business Times-Singapore Regional Index, had helped attract foreign buyers to the Singapore market.
Gainers outnumbered losers by 218 to 122, with Jardine Matheson heading gainers, up US$0.15 to US$6.25.

Dealers said institutional activity was also strong in shipping stocks. Sembawang Corp closed up Singapore $0.35 at S$7.85 on a volume of 3.04 million units and Far East Levingston Shipbuilding, which on Monday boosted its stake in sister company Keppel Engineering, closed up S$0.15 at S$7.45.
